questions.prompt: What is the resonance condition for a series LRC circuit?
State the resonant angular frequency of a series LRC circuit.
At series resonance, what is the impedance of an ideal series LRC circuit?
At resonance, a series circuit has \(R=40\,\Omega\) and \(V_{\mathrm{rms}}=120\,\mathrm V\). Find the rms current.
A series LRC circuit has \(L=0.50\,\mathrm H\) and should resonate at \(100\,\mathrm{Hz}\). Find the required capacitance.
A series resonant circuit has \(L=0.10\,\mathrm H\), \(R=5.0\,\Omega\), and \(f_0=500\,\mathrm{Hz}\). Find \(Q\).
A series circuit has \(\omega_0=2000\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}\) and \(Q=50\). Estimate its bandwidth \(\Delta\omega\).
Explain why the current is maximum at resonance in a series LRC circuit.
questions.answer:
The series impedance is
\[
Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}
\]
At resonance, \(X_L=X_C\), so the reactive part is zero and
\[
Z=R
\]
This is the minimum possible impedance for the circuit, so for fixed source voltage
\[
I=\frac{V}{Z}
\]
is maximum.

questions.prompt: At resonance, a series circuit has \(I_{\mathrm{rms}}=2.0\,\mathrm A\), \(X_L=X_C=300\,\Omega\), and \(R=20\,\Omega\). Find \(V_R\), \(V_L\), \(V_C\), and the source rms voltage.
questions.answer:
Component voltages are
\[
V_R=IR=(2.0)(20)=40\,\mathrm V
\]
\[
V_L=IX_L=(2.0)(300)=600\,\mathrm V
\]
\[
V_C=IX_C=(2.0)(300)=600\,\mathrm V
\]
At resonance, \(V_L\) and \(V_C\) are equal and opposite as phasors, so they cancel in the source phasor sum. The source rms voltage is therefore
\[
V=V_R=40\,\mathrm V
\]
The individual reactive voltages can be much larger than the source voltage.
